thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: @sasha — Dedicated pool exhaustion detected for tenant AcmeHealth (dedicated-pool-acme-us-west-2-42). Severity: P1.

sasha: Seeing the alert. GPUs 0-7 are saturated, queue depth spiking. Confirming whether autoscale is allowed for this pool.

jamal: I can pull metrics. This tenant has reserved 8xA100s, burst cap configured to 2x on-demand but burst currently at 0/2 — looks like we blocked burst due to billing guardrail.

sasha: Can we temporarily allow emergency burst? Customer on enterprise contract — account team needs to sign off but we have a support call in 10m.

acme-liaison: We just got a support page from AcmeHealth — multiple production jobs failing (fraud-scoring pipeline). They are seeing high latency and 429s from our endpoint. They asked for immediate mitigation.

linda: FYI this pool is in the Dedicated tier. Autoscale config: min=8, max=10 (2 burst), cooldown=120s. Billing guardrail prevented auto-burst because monthly commit quota was exceeded for the account.

derek: Uploading the pool status:
```
$ redwoodctl pool describe dedicated-pool-acme-us-west-2-42 --metrics
GPUs: 8/8 allocated
GPU utilization: 98-100%
Queued requests: 412 (median latency 3.2s, 95p 12.6s)
Burst available: 2 (blocked)
Pending scaling events: none
```

emily: Any chance we can evict low-priority tenants? This is a single-tenant dedicated pool — no other tenants. Only option is bumping to on-demand burst or migrating some jobs to shared hosted pool.

sasha: Migration to hosted not ideal — customer data is in a VPC/dedicated pool. Need to avoid pulling data out. Options: 1) enable emergency burst (allow 2x on-demand GPUs) 2) throttle concurrency for non-critical job types 3) coordinate with account team to temporarily increase commit so burst unlocks.

jamal: I checked billing system — account has remaining credit but governance flag set requiring AE approval for additional spend. AE is on call but not immediate. We can override as SRE for P1 but must log approval after.

sasha: I vote enable emergency burst (1 GPU first), hold unit tests and non-prod jobs, and set a rate limit on batch scoring endpoints to protect latency for interactive flows. Assigning tasks: @jamal to flip burst flag, @derek to implement rate limit rules, @linda to notify account team, @acme-liaison to tell customer we're enabling emergency capacity now.

jamal: On it. Running the override now:
```
$ redwoodctl pool set-burst --pool dedicated-pool-acme-us-west-2-42 --enable --count 1 --reason "P1 emergency for AcmeHealth fraud pipeline"
Action: queued
Result: success (burst provisioned 1 GPU)
```

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Burst change recorded (runbook-id: RB-DED-BURST).

derek: Implemented temporary rate limit: 20 rps on /v1/generate for AcmeHealth service-ids. Applied at edge.

sasha: Observing metrics after burst + rate limit:
```
GPU utilization: 92-96%
Queued requests: 210 (median 1.8s, 95p 6.7s)
Error rate (429) down from 6.1% to 0.8%
```

acme-liaison: AcmeHealth reports progress — spike subsiding. They asked how long this will hold.

linda: With 1 extra GPU we have ~40% extra throughput for the heavy models. Should hold for 20-48h depending on traffic. Need AE approval to unlock the second burst GPU or to increase commit for long term.

jamal: AE (Maya) responded via DM approving short-term override for 24h. I documented approval in billing ticket #BILL-8812.

sasha: OK. Next steps: 1) Keep emergency burst enabled for now. 2) Set a scheduled review in 2 hours to reassess. 3) Create a mitigation plan to prevent recurrence (capacity alert threshold change, account-level auto-approve path for enterprise renewals). 4) Postmortem owner: @derek.

derek: I'll own the postmortem. Immediate action items added to incident board:
- Investigate job-level concurrency in customer's pipeline (contact Acme infra team)
- Confirm whether any backfill jobs ran unexpectedly
- Propose default guardrail exceptions for enterprise in billing flow

emily: Handoff note for next on-call: we've enabled 1/2 burst, rate-limited batch endpoints, customer notified, AE approval for 24h logged. Watch for queue build and GPU hours usage. If queue > 300 again, escalate to exec on-call.

sasha: Leaving the incident. Handoff to @emily. Logged in rotation.

emily: Ack — taking over. Will keep monitoring.

incident-bot: :page_facing_up: Incident update logged: INC-2026-ACME-007. Priority: P1. Current status: mitigated (customer degraded -> partial). Next update due in 2h.

acme-liaison: Customer thanks the team and asked for a follow-up architecture review for their scoring pipeline. Scheduling with solutions engineering.

sasha: Thanks everyone. Closing Slack handoff. Postmortem timeline and data to be added by @derek within 3 business days.
